fields.description:
# parity `decision_flips` counts an errored pair as a decision flip

## Context / Problem

An errored side of a paired parity run is scored as a DECISION FLIP. Criterion (b) treats a flip as
never acceptable ("it changes what ships"), so a single transient throttle fails a parity slot as a
model-quality regression.

Proven by experiment through the real entry point (recorded in this ticket's existing comment):
20 gold pairs, both arms unanimous `block`, one v2 record replaced by the production errored record
-> `flips=1, n_gold=20, passed=False`. Re-run end to end through the live driver
`parallel_run_and_diff` (`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:286-302`) with a runner raising
`ThrottlingException` exactly once: identical. One throttle trips four gating failures, including the
never-acceptable criterion.

### The mechanism

`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:107`

    decision_flips = sum(1 for a, b in gold_pairs if a.decision != b.decision)

compares `decision` on both sides of every gold-labelled pair with NO `errored` guard, while an
errored side carries a SYNTHETIC decision no model produced. `err1, err2` are computed at
`parity.py:102` and are unused.

The sole production constructor of an errored record is
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:174`:

    return ItemRecord(valid=False, decision="dropped", errored=True, label=label)

`parity.py:46` documents the contract this violates: `errored` is "a runtime error / timeout (not a
model verdict)". Criterion (d) at `parity.py:128` already gates runtime error rate separately, so
scoring an error under (b) both contradicts `:46` and double-counts one event.

### Two things that look like the mechanism and are NOT

1. It is NOT that the pair survives because `dropped` is a member of `_DECISIONS`. The filter at
   `parity.py:105` is `if a.label in _DECISIONS` — it tests the GOLD LABEL, never `decision`.
   A discriminating experiment gave the errored side `decision="__error__"`, outside `_DECISIONS`,
   and the pair was still retained and counted. NO value of `decision` can exempt an errored pair.
2. It is therefore NOT fixable by changing what `fidelity_spot_eval.py:174` emits; the defect survives
   any value it could pick. That file is out of scope.

The changeable artifact is the missing `errored` guard at `parity.py:107`.

### The silent case

The corroborating validity/error movement that might let a careful reader notice something is off
exists ONLY because `fidelity_spot_eval.py:174` happens to couple `errored=True` with `valid=False`.
Nothing in `ItemRecord` (`parity.py:40-56`) enforces that pairing. A record with
`errored=True, valid=True` yields `flips=1, validity_v2=1.0` — a completely silent fabricated flip.

### The report cannot distinguish fabricated flips from real ones

Three v2 arms against the same v1, all reporting `decision_flips=3` — (A) 3 real / 0 errors,
(B) 2 real + 1 error, (C) 0 real / 3 errors — produce a BYTE-IDENTICAL gating string. `metrics` has
no per-pair detail and no excluded count.

## Approach

Add an `errored` guard to the flip computation at `parity.py:107`: a gold pair where EITHER side has
`errored=True` is excluded from `decision_flips` and counted instead into a new metric
`errored_pairs`, which is surfaced in `ParityReport.metrics` and appended to the flip gating-failure
string so arms (A), (B) and (C) are no longer byte-identical.

The guard reads `a.errored or b.errored` — the field the `parity.py:46` contract already defines as
"not a model verdict" — rather than any decision-vocabulary membership test, because the
discriminating experiment above proved decision-vocabulary tests are a no-op here. Excluding rather
than re-scoring is correct because criterion (d) at `parity.py:128` already gates the error rate: the
event is not lost, it is attributed once to the criterion that owns it instead of twice.

## Scope

* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — guard the `decision_flips` comprehension at `:107`, compute
  `errored_pairs`, add it to the `metrics` dict at `:139-153`, and include it in the flip failure
  string at `:121`. Update the module docstring's criterion (b) wording at `:10-11`.
* `tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py` — add the errored-pair exclusion tests.
* `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` — existing `decision_flips` assertions re-checked; updated only
  where the errored guard legitimately changes an expected value.

## Testing

* An errored pair (production shape `valid=False, decision="dropped", errored=True`) opposite a real
  `block` verdict is excluded from `decision_flips` and reported as errored; RED before the change.
* The silent variant `errored=True, valid=True` is covered specifically, since no other signal
  catches it.
* A genuine flip between two non-errored sides is STILL counted — the guard must not suppress real
  regressions.
* Arms (A) 3 real / 0 errors, (B) 2 real + 1 error and (C) 0 real / 3 errors produce three DIFFERENT
  report outputs, asserted by comparing their gating-failure strings and `errored_pairs` values
  pairwise.
* Each new test is mutation-checked in both directions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An errored pair is excluded from `decision_flips` and reported separately, with the guard at
      `parity.py:107` reading `errored` rather than any decision-vocabulary membership test; verified
      by a unit test asserting `decision_flips == 0` and a non-zero errored count on a one-errored-pair
      run that previously reported `decision_flips == 1`.
- [x] A test constructs a paired run where exactly one side errored and asserts it is not counted as a
      flip; it fails before the fix, verified by running it against the unmodified source.
- [x] A test covers the `errored=True, valid=True` record specifically; it fails before the fix.
- [x] A test asserts a genuine flip between two non-errored sides is still counted, so the guard does
      not mask real regressions.
- [x] Arms (A), (B) and (C) above produce non-identical report output; verified by a test asserting
      pairwise inequality of their gating-failure strings.
- [x] Re-scoring the recorded run at `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json` with this
      guard changes no metric, since that run has a 0.000 error rate on all four arms; verified by an
      offline re-score with zero model calls and recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, and the default test selection is green.
